dataset_metadata.name: ISU-ILCC Battery Aging Dataset
dataset_metadata.institution: University of Connecticut; Iowa State University; University of Oxford; Iowa Lakes Community College
dataset_metadata.citation: Li, T., Zhou, Z., Thelen, A., Howey, D.A., and Hu, C. (2024). Predicting battery lifetime under varying usage conditions from early aging data. Cell Reports Physical Science 5, 101891. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.xcrp.2024.101891
dataset_metadata.funding: Iowa Energy Center grant no. 20-IEC-018; NSF grant no. ECCS-2015710; China Scholarship Council; Department of Engineering Science, University of Oxford

cell_info.cell_notes: 502030-size Li-polymer (lithium polymer) pouch cells manufactured by Honghaosheng Electronics in Shenzhen, China. Operating voltage range 3.0-4.2 V. Rated capacity 250 mAh (1C = 250 mA). Half-cells were assembled from these commercial cells.

aging_modes.notes: Current release contains 238 cells; 13 cells had not completed testing at time of release (Version 2). Four cells cycled per condition to capture cell-to-cell variability. Three stress factors varied: charge C-rate, discharge C-rate, and depth of discharge. Initial conditions selected by grid search (DoD and Cchg, with Cdchg fixed at 0.5 C); later expanded using random sampling across all three factors. Cell lifetimes ranged from 1.5 to 60.9 weeks.

time_protocol.notes: Aging tests consisted of 1-week cycling blocks followed by a weekly RPT. Tests repeated until cell capacity fell below 200 mAh (80% of rated capacity). Maximum observed lifetime was approximately 60.9 weeks. Charge/discharge rates and DoD sampled evenly from 0.5-3 C and 25-100% respectively; actual measured DoD ranged from ~4% to ~100% due to voltage hysteresis effects.

rawdata.data_quality_notes: Q(V) curves from weekly RPTs are the primary data used for feature extraction. Partial DoD cycling data does not allow direct feature extraction from raw cycling data; RPT data used instead.
rawdata.known_issues: Measured DoD values differ from design values due to voltage hysteresis during C/2 discharge used to determine cutoff voltages. Paper reports and discusses actual measured DoD values.

checkup.notes: Each weekly RPT consisted of two complete full-DoD cycles at slow rates (C/2 and C/5) to capture cell voltage response while minimizing kinetic effects. An initial RPT was conducted before aging to determine beginning-of-life health. Features extracted from RPT data include incremental capacity (dQ/dV vs. V) and differential voltage (dV/dQ vs. Q) curves.

notes: The ISU-ILCC dataset was collected jointly by Iowa State University (now University of Connecticut REIL lab) and Iowa Lakes Community College. It is designed to study battery capacity fade as a function of charge rate, discharge C-rate, and depth of discharge. The dataset is unique in its large number of cells (251) under a wide variety of conditions (63 unique), enabling machine learning studies of battery lifetime prediction. The paper (Li et al., Cell Reports Physical Science, 2024) introduces degradation-informed features from incremental capacity curves and a hierarchical Bayesian model for early-life prediction. Version 2 of the dataset adds additional folders and a revised readme (December 2023). Code for feature extraction and modeling is available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.10648587.
